events.comment: Debug keys: one switch (DEBUG_KEYS in the script below) turns every debug key off for the demo. true in development.

inlineCode: // Debug keys: ONE switch for all of them. true = they work (development); false = the demo and release builds, where F2 to F10
// (the bosses' attack triggers, the debug draw, restarting the scene, the hitbox view) and the numpad keys (the Leaf Ranger's
// attack triggers) and the Samurai's 0 key do nothing at all. The game reads keys through gdjs.evtTools.input, so with the
// switch off those keys are made to read as never pressed, once, for the whole game. Combat_Shared is linked by every fight
// and the hub, so this runs wherever a debug key could. Set it to false before building the demo.
input[fn] = function (instanceContainer, key) { return DEBUG.test(String(key)) ? false : original.apply(this, arguments); };

events.comment: Combat_Shared: rules used by every fight. Each scene needs an Enemy group and an EnemyHitbox group, and links this sheet before that boss's own events. Every EnemyHitbox object needs Damage, HasHit and IsMelee variables.
Arena fade-in: every fight (and the tutorial) opens from black: a short hold, then a smooth fade of about a second.

inlineCode: // Arena fade-in: the fight opens from black instead of cutting in. A black sheet over the whole screen (on the
// scene's own top container, so the camera doesn't move it, and it works in scenes without a UI layer) holds for
// HOLD seconds, hiding the first frames while things settle, then fades out over FADE seconds and is removed.
const st = runtimeScene.__arenaFade || (runtimeScene.__arenaFade = { t: 0, sheet: null, done: false });
// Real frame time, capped so a long first (loading) frame doesn't skip the fade.
const k = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (st.t - HOLD) / FADE));
st.sheet.alpha = 1 - k * k * (3 - 2 * k); // Smoothstep: eases in and out.
if (k >= 1) { st.sheet.parent && st.sheet.parent.removeChild(st.sheet); st.sheet.destroy(); st.sheet = null; st.done = true; }

events.comment: Scene start: remember the uncursed max HP and set up the bar maximums. (Where the bars sit is the fight UI layout's job, further down.)
Boss reaction flags: true for one frame. Each boss's events read them right after this sheet.
Remove blood effects when their animation ends.
Remove the deflect spark when its animation ends.
Show the rally bar while rally HP is pending.
Hide the rally bar when no rally HP is pending.
Update every bar value.
Player deleted: empty the HP bar and hide the rally bar.
Cursed HP bar: while cursed, size the black sprite to the max HP lost and pin it to the right end of the HP fill.
Cursed HP bar: no curse, so hide the black sprite.
Curse icons: one flame per curse on the player, in a row next to the stamina bar. Curse_Icon is a tiled sprite, so its width sets how many show.
Curse icons: no curse, so hide them.

Fight UI layout: the player's bars top-left (posture only while above zero), the boss's name, life marks, posture and HP in a block at the bottom centre. It runs after every event each frame, so it overrides where the boss sheets put the bars; they still show and hide them.

inlineCode: // Fight UI layout. In scenes with a UI layer, the bars are laid out after all of the scene's events each frame
// (a post-events callback), so this has the last word on where they sit. The boss sheets still decide when the
// boss bars show (their Show/Hide of Enemy_HP_Bar and Enemy_Posture_Bar); they no longer decide where.
//   Top-left, the player: HP (with rally and the cursed part), stamina, and posture under it; Desperation's icon
//     and count after the curse flames. Posture only shows
//     while it's above zero (fading in and out), and pulses once it's close to breaking.
//   Bottom centre, the boss: name with a mark per life left, posture, and a wide HP bar. The block fades in when
//     the boss sheets show it, and stays hidden through an opening (the Samurai's kneel, rise and bow) and deathblows.
// Scenes without a UI layer (the unfinished Gunslinger) keep their own layout.
// Each boss: its object and the name shown over its bars, by scene.
Samurai_Fight: { obj: "Samurai_NPC", name: "The Samurai", fake: true, trueName: "Two-Shadow", pause: 1.8 },
const OPENING = ["Kneel", "Rise", "Bow"]; // Boss AIStates that keep the boss block hidden.
const HP_W = 560, POSTURE_W = 380, HP_H = 26, POST_H = 22, MARGIN = 12, NAME_SIZE = 16; // Slim bars: they stand on the ground band under the lifted floor.
const one = function (n) { const a = scene.getObjects(n); return a && a.length ? a[0] : null; };
const game = scene.getGame(), W = game.getGameResolutionWidth(), H = game.getGameResolutionHeight();
const st = scene.__fightUIState || (scene.__fightUIState = { boss: 0, posture: 0, t: 0, pips: null });
const toUI = function (o, x, y) { if (o.getLayer() !== "UI") o.setLayer("UI"); o.setX(x); o.setY(y); };
const player = one("Player"), pv = player ? player.getVariables() : null;
// Player posture: under stamina, only while above zero.
const p = pv ? pv.get("Posture").getAsNumber() : 0, mp = pv ? Math.max(1, pv.get("MaxPosture").getAsNumber()) : 1;
const danger = p / mp >= 0.8 ? 0.55 + 0.45 * Math.abs(Math.sin(st.t * 7)) : 1; // Close to breaking: it pulses.
// Desperation: its icon and stack count sit just after the curse flames (Curse_Icon), and pulse when a stack is
// added. Made at runtime the first time a stack appears. Stacks count up to DesperationMax, like the window.
if (pv && pv.has("DespPulse") && pv.get("DespPulse").getAsBoolean()) { pv.get("DespPulse").setBoolean(false); st.despPulse = 1; } // A deflect that needed the Desperation window.
const ci = one("Curse_Icon"), x0 = ci && !ci.isHidden() ? ci.getX() + ci.getWidth() + 5 : 268, y0 = ci ? ci.getY() : 57;
const BASE = 0.85, s = BASE * (1 + 0.35 * st.despPulse); // 15% smaller than the art, pulsing around that size.
di.hide(desp <= 0); di.setScale(s); di.setX(x0 - (s - BASE) * 18); di.setY(y0 - (s - BASE) * 16);
if (dc) { dc.hide(desp <= 0); dc.setCharacterSize(12); const t = "x" + desp; if (dc.getText() !== t) dc.setText(t); dc.setX(x0 + 34); dc.setY(y0 + 7); }
const B = BOSSES[scene.getName()] || null, boss = B ? one(B.obj) : null, bv = boss ? boss.getVariables() : null;
const hp = one("Enemy_HP_Bar"), post = one("Enemy_Posture_Bar"), name = one("Enemy_HP_Text");
const lv = bv && bv.has("Lives") ? Math.round(bv.get("Lives").getAsNumber()) : 0, aiS = bv && bv.has("AIState") ? bv.get("AIState").getAsString() : "";
const bm = bv && bv.has("BarMode") ? bv.get("BarMode").getAsNumber() : 0, cardS = bv && bv.has("CardState") ? bv.get("CardState").getAsNumber() : 0;
// The Samurai's bar must only be gone at his real death: it comes back if something hid it while he is alive.
if (B && B.fake && hp && hp.isHidden() && aiS !== "" && aiS !== "Dead" && OPENING.indexOf(aiS) < 0) { hp.hide(false); if (post) post.hide(false); }

const deathblow = pv && pv.has("IsDeathblow") && pv.get("IsDeathblow").getAsBoolean() && lv <= 1 && bm === 0; // A boss with lives left keeps its bar through a deathblow, and so does the fake death (BarMode 1): only the last one hides it.
const a = 255 * st.boss, hpY = H - MARGIN - HP_H, postY = hpY - POST_H + 3, nameY = postY - NAME_SIZE - 8;
if (hp) { toUI(hp, (W - HP_W) / 2, hpY); hp.setOpacity(a); if (hp.setWidth) { hp.setWidth(HP_W); hp.setHeight(HP_H); } }
if (post) { toUI(post, (W - POSTURE_W) / 2, postY); post.setOpacity(a); if (post.setWidth) { post.setWidth(POSTURE_W); post.setHeight(POST_H); } }
const label = B ? (B.fake && lv === 1 && bm !== 1 ? B.trueName : B.name) : "";
// A small red diamond per life the boss has left, after the name.
if (B && B.fake && lives >= 2) lives -= 1; // The fake last life is not shown: two marks in phase 1, one in phase 2, one for the true form.
if (bm === 1) lives = 0; // "Dead" for the card: no marks.
const x0 = W / 2 + name.getWidth() / 2 + 14, cy = nameY + NAME_SIZE / 2 + 2;
st.pips.beginFill(0x000000, st.boss); st.pips.drawPolygon([cx, cy - 7, cx + 7, cy, cx, cy + 7, cx - 7, cy]); st.pips.endFill();
st.pips.beginFill(0xc8323a, st.boss); st.pips.drawPolygon([cx, cy - 5, cx + 5, cy, cx, cy + 5, cx - 5, cy]); st.pips.endFill();
// The ENEMY DEFEATED card (the Samurai's fakeout): a dark band across the screen with gold lettering. CardState 1 shows it, 2 slashes
// it in half along a diagonal (the halves slide apart and fade), 0 removes it. The Samurai's events decide the timing.
const root = new PIXI.Container(), mid = H * 0.42, ang = 0.42, dx = Math.cos(ang), dy = Math.sin(ang), nx = -dy, ny = dx, cx = W / 2, cy = mid, R = 2000;
const c = new PIXI.Container(), g = new PIXI.Graphics();
g.beginFill(0x8a1c22, 0.95); g.drawRect(0, mid - 80, W, 3); g.drawRect(0, mid + 77, W, 3); g.endFill();
const t = new PIXI.Text("ENEMY DEFEATED", { fontFamily: "Georgia, serif", fontSize: 64, fill: 0xd9c27a, letterSpacing: 10 });
if (t.anchor) t.anchor.set(0.5); t.x = cx; t.y = mid;
const m = new PIXI.Graphics(), sg = s === 0 ? 1 : -1;

m.beginFill(0xffffff, 1); m.drawPolygon([cx - dx * R, cy - dy * R, cx + dx * R, cy + dy * R, cx + dx * R + sg * nx * R, cy + dy * R + sg * ny * R, cx - dx * R + sg * nx * R, cy - dy * R + sg * ny * R]); m.endFill();
halves.push({ c: c, m: m, sg: sg });
st.card = { root: root, halves: halves, flash: flash, t: 0, slash: 0, nx: nx, ny: ny, dx: dx, dy: dy, cx: cx, cy: cy };
if (cardS === 0) { cd.root.destroy({ children: true }); st.card = null; }
const inA = Math.min(1, cd.t / 0.4), s = Math.min(1, cd.slash / 0.5), ease = 1 - (1 - s) * (1 - s), out = cardS === 2 ? 1 - Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (cd.slash - 0.3) / 0.4)) : 1;
const ox = h.sg * cd.nx * 110 * ease, oy = h.sg * cd.ny * 110 * ease;
h.c.x = ox; h.c.y = oy; h.m.x = ox; h.m.y = oy; h.c.alpha = inA * out;

cd.flash.beginFill(0xffffff, fa); cd.flash.drawPolygon([cd.cx - cd.dx * R2 - cd.nx * w, cd.cy - cd.dy * R2 - cd.ny * w, cd.cx + cd.dx * R2 - cd.nx * w, cd.cy + cd.dy * R2 - cd.ny * w, cd.cx + cd.dx * R2 + cd.nx * w, cd.cy + cd.dy * R2 + cd.ny * w, cd.cx - cd.dx * R2 + cd.nx * w, cd.cy - cd.dy * R2 + cd.ny * w]); cd.flash.endFill();
// The old slim bar is retired.
for (const n of ["Enemy_HP_Slim_Back", "Enemy_HP_Slim_Fill"]) { const o = one(n); if (o) o.hide(true); }

events.comment: Enemy posture slowly recovers after 1.5 seconds without being hit.
Keep enemy posture within its maximum.
Enemy dodges this hit: no damage. Sets JustDodgedHit so the boss can react.

Player hits the enemy, once per swing: damage, posture (only if Enemy.MeleeDamagesPosture is true), blood, rally healing, and a hit sound. Sets JustHitByPlayer for the boss's events. Skipped while Enemy.Invulnerable is true. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake.
Melee posture: only for bosses with MeleeDamagesPosture on. The Gunslinger has it off, so sword hits only cost it health and its posture comes from parried bullets.
The hit came from a lunge: add LungeBonusDamage and set JustStaggered for the boss events.
Enemy posture break: starts the stun and sets JustPostureBroken for the boss's events. Also adds a strong hit-stop and screen shake.
Enemy stun ends after Enemy.StunDuration seconds and sets JustRecovered for the boss's events.

Deathblow: press F in melee range of a posture-broken enemy. The player winds up, then cuts. The cut removes one enemy life, and the curse lifts as the life wisps reach the player. The player is locked and cannot be hit until it finishes. Also adds a strong hit-stop and screen shake on the cut.
Enemy on the right: dash right.
Enemy on the left: dash left.
Wall check: pass through only if the landing spot, DeathblowPassDist past the enemy, is inside DeathblowMinX to DeathblowMaxX. Otherwise the cut happens in front of him and the player stays put.
Room behind the enemy: pass through.
Deathblow cut, on the dash frame: the hit itself, the orb shatter and the slash. The player then glows crimson as the life is taken.
Pass through: land DeathblowPassDist past the enemy, still facing the same way, so the player ends with their back to him. The slash runs from where they started to where they land.
Wall behind the enemy: no pass. The slash runs from the player across the enemy.
Deathblow: hold the follow-through, blade forward, for DeathblowHold seconds.
Deathblow: the hold is over, so he raises the blade, slowly, to clean it.
Deathblow: the blade is up. Pause there for DeathblowRaiseHold seconds, the moment before the flick.
Deathblow: the pause is over, so flick the blood off in one fast swish, then settle.
Deathblow finished: give control back.

Deathblow glow: for DeathblowGlowTime seconds the player glows crimson, fading back, as the stolen life flows in. When it ends, the curse lifts and HP refills (DeathblowLanded, handled by the curse removal event below).
Early in the glow: deep crimson.
Later in the glow: fading toward normal.
Glow over: back to normal, and the life lands.
Remove the orb shatter and the slash when their animations end.
Remove the slash when its animation ends.
Deathblow prompt: the orb, hidden by default. Uses the same conditions as the deathblow, minus the key press.
Deathblow prompt: show the orb just above the enemy's head when a deathblow is possible. Enemy.DeathblowOrbDrop lowers it for a boss whose stunned pose is shorter than its collision box.
Enemy loses a life at 0 HP and sets JustLostLife. On its last life it is deleted, or sets JustDied if HasDeathAnimation is on.

Debug, left Alt: toggle Desperation. On: put the player on his last life with every curse stack (4 of the 5 lives lost, 15% max HP each, full HP of what is left), and remember what he had (DbgLives, DbgCurse, DbgMaxHealth, DbgHealth). Off (press again): give those back. The next hit kills while it is on. Remove before release (DEBUG_KEYS). DbgSnap is taken first, so the on and off events cannot both run in one frame (the off event used to undo the on event at once).

Desperation: the curse's silver lining. Each curse stack, up to DesperationMax (3), widens the deflect window by DesperationStep (0.02 s), so a struggling player gets a little more forgiveness. Boss timings are unchanged, and the curse still costs max HP, so dying is never the better way to play. Both deflects (this sheet's and the Gunslinger's) read DeflectWindowNow; the icon is drawn by the fight UI layout below.

Directional deflecting, for every fight: a deflect only counts when the player faces the boss (facing left means FlippedX). FacingOk is 1 unless the player has their back to him. Not applied (stays 1) when DirectionalDeflect on the Player is 0, when the boss has DeflectAnySide 1 (his sheet sets it while an attack comes from several sides, for example the boss is hidden or dead), or when he is within 40 px sideways. Each attack also has its own Directional variable (1 normal, 0 for attacks that come from all around, like the petals and the arrow rain), read by the deflect event below.

Deflect: an enemy attack that reaches the player within DeflectWindowNow seconds (DeflectWindow, widened by Desperation) of raising the sword is stopped, with a random clash sound and a burst of sparks (one of the Deflect_Spark animations, picked at random). Setting HasHit makes the damage event below skip it. All enemy attacks go through this, including each Thousand Cuts slash. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake. One press stops any number of melee attacks, but only one ranged attack (DeflectRangedUsed), so each arrow of a double shot needs its own deflect. Both branches of that Or name EnemyHitbox and Player on purpose: an Or only keeps the objects its true branches picked, so a branch that left one out would drop it (no arrow blocked, or no Player to act on). A hitbox with SharedDeflect 1 (the Samurai's paired mirror cuts, his waves of petals) does not use up the press: it counts like a melee attack for this, but adds no posture, so one deflect stops everything of that kind that reaches the player in the window. Directional deflecting: unless the attack's Directional variable is 0, the press only counts when the player faces the boss (Player.FacingOk, worked out just above).

Deflect sound: one of the 21 echo clashes at random (7 pitches x 3 takes, made by tools/fx/clash.js), so repeated deflects never sound identical. Replaces sword_parry_01.wav. Also draws the new spark additively, so its glow lights up its surroundings.

inlineCode: // Deflect sound: a random echo clash. The files are deflect_clash_<pitch>_echo[_b|_c].wav in assets/Sfx,
// generated by tools/fx/clash.js (rerun it to change them). Volume 51: 40% under the old parry sound (85), which was too loud with these.
// Spark light: the new Deflect_Spark is drawn additively, so its glow halo brightens what is behind it like real light.
for (const s of runtimeScene.getObjects("Deflect_Spark")) if (!s.__lit) { s.__lit = true; s.setBlendMode(1); }

events.comment: Deflected a melee attack: it also adds DeflectPostureDamage to the enemy posture and stops posture recovery for a moment, like a hit does. Attacks with IsMelee off, such as ranged ones, add nothing.
Deflected a ranged attack (an arrow, a rain hit): this press is used up for ranged attacks, so a second arrow close behind it needs its own deflect.

Desperation feedback: the deflect landed after the base DeflectWindow, so only the curse's extra window allowed it. Flag it for the blade glow and the icon pulse (a deflect inside the normal window shows nothing).

Enemy attack hits the player once per attack object. Damage comes from that object's Damage variable, and JustHitPlayer is set for the boss's events. A hit also drops any saved action, cancels the player attack, deflect or roll (a roll only gets hit once its i-frames are over) and plays the Player_Hit reaction. Also adds hit-stop and screen shake. Nothing can hit the player during a grab, so a stray attack cannot break that animation.
Player loses a life: applies the curse (one more CurseStacks), clears rally and posture, and starts respawn invulnerability. On the last life, the player dies instead.
Last life gone: play the death animation. The player is locked and cannot be hit, and the fade below returns to the hub.
End respawn invulnerability after 1.5 seconds.
Player death: DeathHold seconds after the collapse, fade the screen to black over DeathFadeTime seconds.
Player death fade: darken, keep it over the camera, and go back to the hub once it is black.
Player death fade is black: back to the hub.
Curse removal: the deathblow sets Player.DeathblowLanded. This restores max HP, clears CurseStacks, refills HP, and clears rally.
Player status, root: while RootLeft lasts the player cannot move, roll or lunge, but can still attack and deflect. Player_Movement checks IsRooted.
Root over.
Player status, poison: while PoisonLeft lasts, the player loses PoisonTick HP every half second and is tinted purple. Death ends it.
Every half second: lose PoisonTick HP. PoisonAcc counts the time, because a timer that was never started never passes its check.
Poison over: back to the normal colour.
Debug: F5 restarts the current scene. Remove before release.

Boss beaten: when every enemy in the Enemy group is dead and its death animation has settled, wait a moment, fade to black, mark the boss as beaten (BossesBeaten), note this fight in JustBeaten (the hub starts the player at its gate) and return to HUB_Area.

inlineCode: // Boss beaten: once every enemy in the scene's Enemy group has died and settled (its death animation on its last frame,
// or deleted), wait HOLD seconds, fade to black over FADE seconds and go back to the hub.
// Scenes that never had a living enemy (the hub, the templates) never trigger it. A dying player wins over it.
const HOLD = 2.5; // Seconds to look at the fallen boss before the fade.
const FADE = 1.2; // Seconds for the fade to black.
const MAX_SETTLE = 20; // Seconds: stop waiting for a death animation that never reaches its last frame.
const st = runtimeScene.__victory || (runtimeScene.__victory = { names: null, seen: false, settle: 0, hold: 0, fade: 0, overlay: null });
for (const name of st.names) for (const o of runtimeScene.getObjects(name)) {
if (runtimeScene.getObjects("Player_Death_Fade").length > 0) return; // The player died too: the death fade handles it.
const dt = time.getElapsedTime() / 1000 / time.getTimeScale(); // Real seconds, through hit-stops.
if (dying > 0 && st.settle < MAX_SETTLE) { st.settle += dt; return; }
// Fade: a black rectangle over everything, on the UI layer (or the base layer in scenes without one).
// Remember the win for the hub, which shows this boss's gate as completed (until the game is closed).
// And which fight we just won, so the hub can start the player at its gate and play the defeat cutscene.

events.comment: Desperation glow: the player's blade glows teal for 0.3 s when a deflect only landed thanks to the Desperation window.

inlineCode: // Desperation glow: when a deflect landed only because Desperation widened the window (the Player's DespUsed flag, set by the
// deflect event), the player's blade glows teal for 0.3 s: an additive halo at the Blade point that swells a little and fades.
// The same press also pulses the Desperation icon (DespPulse, read by the fight UI below). Real time, so it lasts through the hit-stop.
const st = runtimeScene.__despGlow || (runtimeScene.__despGlow = { g: null, t: 0, x: 0, y: 0 });
st.g.blendMode = 1; // Additive, like the deflect spark.
st.g.zIndex = 1000000; // On top of the fighters (the layer sorts by zIndex), or the sprites hide it.
const k = Math.max(0, st.t / GLOW_TIME), grow = 1 + (1 - k) * 0.6;
for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) { st.g.beginFill(COLOR, 0.22 * k); st.g.drawCircle(st.x, st.y, (10 + i * 7) * grow); st.g.endFill(); }

events.comment: Arena lift: the camera rests 48 px lower, so the arena sits higher and the boss bars have the ground band to themselves. Runs before the shake, which rests around the same base.

inlineCode: // Arena lift: the fight camera rests LIFT px lower in the world, so the arena (floor and fighters) sits LIFT px higher on
// screen and the boss bars at the bottom stand on the ground band under the floor instead of cutting into it. The floor
// has extra tile rows to fill the gap. The shake below rests around runtimeScene.__cameraBase, so this sets it. The hub
// sets its own (a following camera), so it is left alone. The UI layer is not moved.
const base = { x: game.getGameResolutionWidth() / 2, y: game.getGameResolutionHeight() / 2 + LIFT };

events.comment: Hit-stop and screen shake: runs last, so effects started on this frame apply right away. Tune them with the HitStop and Shake variables on the Player.

inlineCode: // Hit-stop and screen shake. Events start them by setting HitStopLeft, ShakeLeft and ShakeStrength on the Player, in real seconds.
const STOP_TIME_SCALE = 0.05; // Game speed during a hit-stop. Not 0, so the elapsed time stays usable.
const SHAKE_LAYERS = ["Background", ""]; // The UI layer stays still.
// Where the camera rests when not shaking. A scene with a moving camera (the hub's follow) sets runtimeScene.__cameraBase
// each frame before this runs, so the shake happens around it. Fight scenes don't, so they rest at the screen centre.
const base = runtimeScene.__cameraBase || { x: centerX, y: centerY };
// Player deleted: nothing can end the effects any more, so end them here.
// Elapsed time is scaled by the game speed, so undo that to count in real seconds.
